messages:
alex_runtime: :wave: Ran the P95-driven batching experiment this morning (queue-sampler + dynamic token quota per-route). Mixed results — throughput up ~12% but p95 jumped on a subset of small routes. Posting quick notes and profiling output, open to ideas.

maria_perf: Can you paste the canary numbers and the profile snapshots?

alex_runtime: Canary summary:
- baseline p95: 210ms -> experiment p95: 320ms
- p50: ~stable (85ms -> 92ms)
- overall RPS ~+10-15%
- KV cache hit rate: 82% -> 68% (big drop on routes with median seq < 30)
Suspect batching alignment + kernel switch behavior.

jamal: Did the kernel selector change recently? We had the fused-attn preference landed last week for short sequences.

tess_eng: Yes — kernel-selector now prefers fused-attn when microbatch > 1 and seq <= 128. That was meant to speed medium batches but might increase switch overhead.

alex_runtime: Current batcher config we tested:
```
queue_sampler:
  max_batch_size: 64
  microbatch_target: 8
  token_budget_per_batch: route_dynamic
route_token_budget_policy:
  default: 64
  enterprise: 96
  free: 48
```

maria_perf: Profile takeaways: flamegraphs show extra scheduling gaps around kernel boundary (context switch + kernel upload) for many small-route requests. Also KV cache evictions ticked up because microbatches are breaking prefix reuse — effective cache locality worsened.

jamal: Wait — did we change when KV lookup happens relative to microbatch formation? If KV lookup moved after microbatching that could explain duplicate CP entries and misses.

tess_eng: We did move KV cache check to after microbatch formation to reduce duplicate work in hot routes, but that had an unintended effect: microbatches for short sequences ended up not reusing the same KV payload across microbatches because we only checked once per batch. That's a bug.

sre_bot: [alert] canary-run 2003456805: p95 violation for route `/search-small` (threshold=250ms). 3 consecutive windows.

kelly_prod: Noticed customers on enterprise tier saw much smaller regresses — looks correlated with route_tier. Free/low-priority routes hit the worst tail.

alex_runtime: Quick mitigation ideas:
1) Revert KV lookup placement (do KV check per microbatch) for short-seq routes.
2) Add hysteresis to kernel selector so fused-attn only used when seq distribution > 48 AND microbatch >= 4.
3) Adjust dynamic token budget formula to prefer smaller microbatching on short routes.

maria_perf: For token budget, propose this per-route formula to test (A/B):
```
# per-route token budget tune (pseudo)
median = observed_median_context(route, last_5m)
budget = clamp(round(median * 1.25), 32, 128)
if route_tier == 'enterprise': budget = min(160, round(budget * 1.25))
```
Expect: short routes keep small budgets, reducing microbatch packing latency; long-chat routes still get efficiency.

jamal: Also suggest measuring kernel-switch latency explicitly and gating fused-attn when the measured overhead > 8ms for the microbatch shape. Adds a small runtime cost but avoids tail spikes.

alex_runtime: Plan: revert KV-placement fix in canary, add kernel hysteresis, and run targeted 10% route-tier canary split (targeting free + small routes). If p95 improves back toward baseline, then roll rollout and ship refined token_budget formula.

deploy-bot: Command executed: `deploy rollback canary-batcher-config --tag=2003456799`
deploy-bot: Output: rollback started -> canary nodes 3/3 rolled back -> health checks passing.

maria_perf: For the canary you'll want these metrics instrumented: per-route p95, per-route KV_hit_rate, kernel_switch_latency histogram, microbatch_stall_ratio. Plot them in the perf dashboard and set temporary alert at p95 > 260ms for the canary group.

jamal: Also add a short-circuit in the sampler: if median_seq < 24, cap microbatch_target to 2 unless enterprise. That should reduce tail packing.

alex_runtime: I'll open a PR for KV-placement revert + kernel hysteresis + token budget formula and include the microbatch cap. Starting a 10% canary in ~30m. Tagging @oncall for watch :eyes:.

kelly_prod: Thanks — please ping if you need a rollback. Will monitor enterprise SLAs.

alex_runtime: Thanks everyone — follow-up sync in #eng-runtime tomorrow to review canary traces and decide final thresholds.
